definitions.explanation: Paper treated with oil to make it water-resistant. Traditionally used to wrap goods, line umbrellas and raincoats, and keep out moisture before plastics became common.

examples.japanese: {油紙|あぶらがみ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{包|つつ}む→包む：01226_tsutsumu⟧。
⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{傘|かさ}→傘：00639_kasa⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{油紙|あぶらがみ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{作|つく}られていた→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: Umbrellas in the old days were made from oilpaper.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧な⟦{書類|しょるい}→書類：01103_shorui⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{油紙|あぶらがみ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{包|つつ}んで→包む：01226_tsutsumu⟧⟦{湿気|しっけ}→湿気：03177_shikke⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{守|まも}った→守る：01986_mamoru⟧。
examples.english: I wrapped the important documents in oilpaper to protect them from moisture.

notes:
Paper soaked or coated with drying oil so that it repels water. Once everywhere in daily life—on ⟦{番傘|ばんがさ}→番傘：06295_bangasa⟧ (traditional umbrellas), raincoats, and packaging—it is now largely replaced by plastic and vinyl.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {油紙|あぶらがみ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{包|つつ}む→包む：01226_tsutsumu⟧: to wrap in oilpaper
- {油紙|あぶらがみ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{火|ひ}→火：02248_hi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧つく: oilpaper catches fire — also an idiom for someone who talks on and on once they get started

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {蝋紙|ろうがみ}: waxed paper — coated with wax rather than oil
- ⟦ビニール→ビニール：11140_biniiru⟧: vinyl — the modern waterproof material that replaced oilpaper
